extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural rules for submitting computer program listings, large tables, sequence listings, and Information Disclosure Statements in U.S. patent applications (formats, size/line thresholds, labeling, amendment procedures, and related publication/treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing submission thresholds and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing contained on three hundred printout lines or less may be submitted either as drawings, as part of the written specification, as an ASCII text file on a read-only optical disc, or as an ASCII text file via the USPTO patent electronic filing system. A computer program listing contained on 301 printout lines or more must be submitted as an ASCII plain text file on a read-only optical disc or submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system. A listing of over 60 lines and not more than 300 lines, if submitted as part of the specification, must be positioned at the end of the specification and before the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.64.01 and 6.64.02 are to be used to notify applicants. If >300 lines included in the descriptive portion of specification (filed on/after Sept 8, 2000), require conversion to a Computer Program Listing Appendix (text file via EFS or read-only optical disc) and insert appropriate reference at beginning of specification. For >60 and ≤300 lines included as printout, either incorporate as text file via EFS/disc or place the listing after detailed description but before claims. See 37 CFR 1.96 and MPEP § 608.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix technical compatibility and character requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' must be compatible with PC or Mac computers and with MS-DOS, MS-Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux operating systems; may only have ASCII CRLF or LF line terminators; data must not depend on control characters or codes not defined in the ASCII character set; and must have a file name with a '.txt' extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements derived from 37 CFR 1.96(c)(1)-(2). Ensure the file uses only ASCII printable characters (and permitted line terminators) and does not rely on special/nonstandard control codes so the Office can view contents across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix file size, compression, and splitting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a 25 MB size limit for Computer Program Listing Appendix files submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; file compression is not permitted for EFS submissions. It may be possible to break up files larger than 25 MB into multiple files of 25 MB or less. Read-only optical disc submissions may be compressed (WinZip, 7-Zip, Unix/Linux Zip) and must not be self-extracting. Nested file structures must be compressed; if compressed file still does not fit on single disc, it may be split into multiple parts per target disc size and labeled per 37 CFR 1.52(e)(5)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EFS for single-file submissions ≤25 MB without compression; for larger program listings consider splitting into multiple text files (each ≤25 MB) for EFS, or use read-only optical discs with allowable compression and labeling rules. Do not submit self-extracting archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate read-only optical disc submission and labeling (program listings and large tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-only optical discs containing a Computer Program Listing Appendix or 'Large Tables' must be submitted in duplicate and labeled as 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2' respectively. The transmittal letter accompanying the discs must state that the two discs are identical. If the two copies are not identical, the Office will use the disc labeled 'Copy 1' for further processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate copies required because OPAP retains one for records and one for the examiner. Differences between copies may cause the Office to select Copy 1 for processing. Ensure exact duplication and proper labeling to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/replacement procedure for computer listings on read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: To amend a Computer Program Listing Appendix submitted on a read-only optical disc, a replacement ASCII plain text file must be submitted via the EFS or on a read-only optical disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e). Replacement discs must be submitted in duplicate and labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'. A request must be made that the material in the replacement file be incorporated by reference in a separate paragraph of the specification identifying the file name, date of creation, and size in bytes. A statement identifying location of all deletions and a statement that the replacement contains no new matter must also be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial submission was on disc, amendments cannot be made via EFS (except by submitting replacement disc). Include explicit labeling, incorporation-by-reference language (37 CFR 1.77(b)(5)), and certification statements about deletions and absence of new matter. The Office may require replacement if discs are corrupted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirement for ASCII/plain text appendices and effect on original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An ASCII plain text 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' or 'Large Tables' must be appropriately referenced in the specification by a separate paragraph incorporating by reference the material (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5)). A Computer Program Listing Appendix filed as an ASCII plain text file on the application filing date is treated as part of the originally filed disclosure even if the incorporation-by-reference statement is omitted; examiners should require insertion of the statement if omitted and may insert it by examiner's amendment when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification contains the separate incorporation paragraph naming the file, date, and size. If omitted but the file was filed on the application filing date, the Office treats it as part of the original disclosure, but applicants should proactively include the incorporation paragraph to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and thresholds for 'Large Tables' eligible for ASCII plain text submission
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Large Tables' that may be submitted in electronic form in ASCII plain text are: (1) any individual table that is more than 50 pages in length; or (2) multiple tables where the total number of pages of all tables in an application exceeds 100 pages (a table page is a page printed on paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presentation of a subheading to divide a large table into smaller sections should not be used to avoid electronic submission unless subdivided tables are presented as numerous files so as to lose relation to the overall large table. Single tables ≤50 pages or multiple tables totaling ≤100 pages must be submitted as drawings, as part of the specification on paper, or via EFS per the Legal Framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Tables spatial relationship and ASCII/plain-text content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted in ASCII plain text must maintain the spatial relationships (alignment of columns and rows) of table elements when displayed; must be compatible with PC or Mac and MS-DOS, MS-Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux operating systems; must be ASCII plain text with all printable characters permitted and no nonprintable ASCII control characters except CRLF or LF as line terminators; must be named as *.txt with file name restrictions (letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, no spaces or other chars, not exceed 60 characters excluding extension); and must be incorporated by reference in a separate paragraph of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care that row/column alignment is preserved when the file is opened at the Office to allow viewing with virtually any text viewer. Use only permitted characters and proper line terminators. Choose file names that meet character and length restrictions and clearly indicate which table each file contains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Tables file size, compression, and submission method rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted via EFS must not exceed 25 MB and file compression is not permitted. Large Tables submitted on read-only optical disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e) may be compressed using WinZip, 7-Zip, or Unix/Linux Zip (not self-extracting) and, if still too large, may be split into multiple file parts and labeled per 37 CFR 1.52(e)(5)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer EFS for files ≤25 MB (no compression). For larger files, use read-only optical discs with allowed compression and proper labeling/splitting. Be mindful of the Office's electronic filing limits and the Legal Framework guidance for splitting files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/replacement requirements for Large Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments to Large Tables in electronic ASCII plain text must include: (1) a replacement ASCII plain text file submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc labeled 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'; (2) a request that the amendment be made by incorporation by reference in a separate paragraph of the specification identifying file name, date, and size in bytes; (3) a statement identifying location of all deletions, replacements, or additions; and (4) a statement that the replacement file contains no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the information was originally filed on read-only optical disc, amendments cannot be made using EFS but must be made by replacement disc. Follow labeling conventions and provide the required statements to allow the Office to identify changes and to ensure no new matter is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and publication of lengthy tables in patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When lengthy tables (tables on >200 consecutive pages or large numbers of tables) are submitted on read-only optical disc or as text files via EFS or in an electronic format (XML, tab-delimited, Excel, Word, etc.), these lengthy tables will not be published as part of the patent document. Instead, a standardized 'LENGTHY TABLE' statement will be inserted in the patent document with reference to the external electronic copy, and the tables will be published separately on the USPTO sequence homepage (seqdata.uspto.gov) with instructions for access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For embedded lengthy tables available electronically, the patent or publication will contain a single-column 'LENGTHY TABLE' placeholder and refer readers to the USPTO website or to an available electronic copy (and fee-based retrieval) rather than printing the tables in the patent document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting rules for printed chemical and mathematical formulas and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical and mathematical formulas and tables must be presented in compliance with § 1.52(a) and (b); may be placed in landscape orientation if necessary; typewritten characters must be from a block (nonscript) font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier) with capital letters preferably at least 0.422 cm (0.166 inches) high (font size ~12 points) but not smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inches) high (~6 points). A space at least 0.64 cm (0.25 inches) high should be provided between complex formulas and tables and the text. Tables should have lines and columns closely spaced to conserve space while maintaining legibility. Formulas must maintain proper positioning of characters to preserve meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use block fonts and sufficiently large font sizes to ensure legibility; provide adequate vertical space between formulas/tables and surrounding text. Landscape orientation is permitted when portrait cannot satisfactorily present the data. Maintain character positioning to preserve chemical/mathematical meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective form-paragraph actions for table non-compliance (less than 51 pages, misalignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a description contains a table of less than 51 pages submitted only as ASCII text file via EFS/disc (contrary to 37 CFR 1.58(c)(1)), applicant must cancel text-file references, file a paper version in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52 or file a PDF via EFS, and change references accordingly. If table column/row relationships are not maintained in an ASCII text table (data misaligned), applicant is required to submit a replacement text file with proper alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.63.01 (table <51 pages submitted only as text file) and 6.63.02 (column/row relationship not maintained) are used to notify applicants. In bracketed form paragraphs insert page ranges or specific misaligned areas. Ensure tables preserve alignment and follow size thresholds for ASCII submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing format requirements by application filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences are required to provide sequence information in a sequence listing. For applications filed before July 1, 2022, the sequence listing can be an ASCII plain text 'Sequence Listing' in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821-1.824 and must be submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc. For applications filed on or after July 1, 2022, the sequence listing must be a 'Sequence Listing XML' file in compliance with 37 CFR 1.831-1.834 and can be submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP §§ 2420 et seq. (pre-2022) and §§ 2412-2419 (post-2022) for detailed formatting and submission rules. Use the appropriate sequence listing format corresponding to filing date and ensure submission via accepted media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) timing windows and conditions for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS will be considered by the Office if filed by the applicant within specified periods: (1) within three months of the filing date of a national application (other than a CPA under § 1.53(d)); (2) within three months of entry of the national stage in an international application; (3) before mailing of a first Office action on the merits; (4) before mailing of a first Office action after a request for continued examination (RCE); or (5) within three months of publication of the international registration in certain international design applications. If filed after those periods, an IDS may still be considered if filed before mailing of any final action/notice of allowance/other closing action and accompanied by either the statement specified in paragraph (e) or the fee per § 1.17(p). If filed even later (but on or before payment of issue fee), it will be considered only if accompanied by the paragraph (e) statement and the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions of time under § 1.136 are permitted for filing an IDS. If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with § 1.98 but parts are inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance. An IDS is not a representation that a search has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement required contents and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must state either a heading that clearly indicates the list is an information disclosure statement and include legible copies of: (i) each foreign patent; (ii) each publication or the portion causing it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (iii) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and any drawing or the portion causing the listing; and (iv) all other information or the portion that caused it to be listed. The statement must also include one of two certifications: (1) that each item was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the IDS; or (2) that no item was cited in a foreign patent office communication and, to the knowledge of the signer after reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDS must be complete and include the specified legible copies and appropriate certification. Use the correct heading and ensure the signer has made reasonable inquiry as required by § 1.98(e)(2). If items were cited by a foreign office within three months, use the corresponding certification option. Attach required copies and ensure procedural compliance to have the IDS considered.
